cleanIntro: The Governor is covered by the J/K/L/N revolver book plus its own appendix, and that book publishes no disassembly at all — cleaning is done with the revolver whole and the cylinder swung out. Most of the care this gun needs is in what you put in it and in the moon clips that make 45 ACP work.

steps.title: Confirm this is the right book — not the BODYGUARD 38 or the X-Frame
steps.action: Check that the revolver in front of you is a Governor and that you are not holding an M&P BODYGUARD 38 or an X-Frame 460 or 500 Magnum. Smith & Wesson publishes separate manuals for those, and nothing in this one is written for them.
steps.prose: The Governor rides on a scandium-alloy N-size frame with a long cylinder for 410 shotshells, so it is covered here alongside the J, K, L and N-Frame revolvers, with a dedicated appendix of its own at page 27. The model name and number sit inside the yoke and are only readable with the cylinder open, which is the first thing you are about to do anyway.
steps.quote: There are separate manuals for S&W® BODYGUARD® 38 and X-FRAME 460 & 500 Magnum revolvers - available free upon request or via download from our web site.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
Revolvers
- Modern Style - J, K, L and N Frame - — p/n 416560000 REV:S&W_REVOLVER_112119 — Cover page, p.1

steps.title: Thumbpiece forward, cylinder out, check all six charge holes
steps.action: With your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard, press the thumbpiece fully forward and hold it, then push the cylinder out to the left. Verify that every charge hole is free of live ammunition and that the bore is clear.
steps.prose: Hold the thumbpiece forward for the whole swing or the cylinder stop drags in its notch. On a Governor a charge hole can be holding any of three very different things — a 410 shell, a 45 Colt, or a 45 ACP on a clip — and a short 45 ACP sits deep enough in that long chamber to be easy to overlook from the front of the cylinder, so look in from the rear.
steps.quote: You must verify that all charge holes (chambers) are free of live ammunition and that the bore is free of obstructions.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
Revolvers
- Modern Style - J, K, L and N Frame - — p/n 416560000 REV:S&W_REVOLVER_112119 — Inspecting Your Revolver, p.15

steps.title: Muzzle up, extractor rod through, count what falls
steps.action: Hold the cylinder out, point the barrel upward in a safe direction and press the extractor rod through the cylinder, then count what you recover against the charge holes.
steps.prose: Muzzle up is what stops a partly lifted case sliding back down its hole to read as empty, and the Governor's chambers are long enough to hide one. Anything that was loaded on a moon clip comes out still attached to the clip rather than dropping loose, so 'nothing fell out' is not proof the gun is empty.
steps.quote: Carefully count the cartridges or spent casings to be sure that you have recovered all of them.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
Revolvers
- Modern Style - J, K, L and N Frame - — p/n 416560000 REV:S&W_REVOLVER_112119 — Unloading, p.25

steps.title: 45 ACP, 45 Colt and 410 shotshells — nothing else
steps.action: The Governor is chambered to fire 45 ACP, 45 Colt and 410 gauge shotshells interchangeably and nothing else. Check the barrel marking for the shotshell length your gun takes — 2 1/2 inch on the standard Governor — and never force a 410 shell into a charge hole; if a brand does not drop in easily, use a different brand.
steps.prose: This is a three-cartridge chamber, which makes it unusually easy to feed something that fits and should not be there. Length is the trap with 410: a 3 inch shell will start into a 2 1/2 inch chamber and jam the crimp into the forcing cone, which is why the manual tells you to read the barrel rather than the box.
steps.quote: S&W® GOVERNOR® REVOLVERS ARE CHAMBERED TO FIRE, INTERCHANGEABLY, 45 ACP*, 45 COLT, AND 410 GAUGE SHOTSHELLS ONLY. NEVER USE A CARTRIDGE NOT SPECIFICALLY DESIGNATED FOR USE IN YOUR FIREARM. OTHER CARTRIDGES MAY FIT INTO THE CHAMBERS OF THE CYLINDER, HOWEVER, FAILURE TO USE THE CORRECT TYPE, CALIBER/GAUGE, OR LENGTH OF AMMUNITION MAY CAUSE THE FIREARM TO JAM, FAIL TO FIRE, OR EVEN GENERATE EXCESSIVE PRESSURE WHICH CAN RUPTURE THE FIREARM
steps.cite:

steps.warn: 45 ACP, 45 COLT and 410 gauge shotshells only.

steps.title: 45 Auto Rim must NOT be used in a Governor
steps.action: Do not load 45 Auto Rim in this revolver. Smith & Wesson prints that restriction three separate times in this manual — in the ammunition section, in the ammunition-continued section and again in the Governor appendix — and it is specific to the Governor, not general advice.
steps.prose: 45 Auto Rim exists precisely so that a rimmed 45 can be fired in a revolver without a clip, so it is the obvious thing to reach for and it is exactly what is barred here. The Governor's charge holes are cut for the rimless 45 ACP on clips and for the much longer 410 shell, and the Auto Rim's thick rim does not belong in that geometry.
steps.quote: 45 Auto Rim cartridges must NOT be used in the S&W® GOVERNOR® revolvers.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
Revolvers
- Modern Style - J, K, L and N Frame - — p/n 416560000 REV:S&W_REVOLVER_112119 — Ammunition, p.9; repeated p.12 and in the Governor Appendix, p.27
steps.warn: 45 Auto Rim cartridges must NOT be used in the S&W GOVERNOR revolvers.

steps.title: Moon clips: two-round or full six-round only, never half moon
steps.action: 45 ACP goes into this revolver only on moon clips — two-round clips or full six-round clips. Half Moon three-round clips should not be used in the Governor, and rimless cartridges in any Smith & Wesson revolver need clips at all (the M547 being the one exception the manual names).
steps.prose: The clip is a headspacing part here, not a loading convenience: without it a rimless 45 ACP runs forward in the long chamber, giving light strikes and leaving nothing for the ejector star to catch. The two-round clips are what let you mix 45 ACP with loose 45 Colt and 410 shells in the same cylinder, which is the Governor's whole point.
steps.caution: Half Moon (3-ROUND) clips should not be used in the S&W® GOVERNOR® Revolver.
steps.quote: If rimless cartridges are to be used in a Smith & Wesson revolver, moon clips must be used (except in Smith & Wesson M547 revolvers) to ensure correct cartridge position for both firing and extraction. Failure to use moon clips with rimless cartridges may result in a malfunction of the revolver.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
Revolvers
- Modern Style - J, K, L and N Frame - — p/n 416560000 REV:S&W_REVOLVER_112119 — Ammunition, p.12

steps.title: Nothing marked +P+, and no light Magnum bullets in an alloy cylinder
steps.action: Ammunition marked +P+ must not be used in Smith & Wesson firearms. Separately, if your revolver has a titanium alloy cylinder, do not use Magnum loads with bullet weights of less than 120 grains.
steps.prose: The +P+ objection is that the marking names no defined pressure limit at all, so two boxes wearing it can be far apart in what they generate. The 120-grain rule is about a different failure entirely — a very light bullet leaves the case early and lets flame cut at the front of the charge holes, and on a titanium alloy cylinder that erosion is not recoverable and voids the warranty.
steps.caution: "Plus-P-Plus" (+P+) ammunition must not be used in Smith & Wesson firearms.
steps.quote: Do not use Magnum loads with bullet weights of less than 120 grains - This will reduce the possibility of premature erosion in titanium alloy cylinders.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL
Revolvers
- Modern Style - J, K, L and N Frame - — p/n 416560000 REV:S&W_REVOLVER_112119 — Ammunition Selection for Lightweight Revolvers, CAUTION, p.13

steps.title: The barrel is not yours to remove
steps.action: Leave the barrel alone. On a barrel/barrel-shroud revolver the stainless steel barrel tube comes out only in a qualified gunsmith's hands with a special tool from Smith & Wesson, and it goes back with that same tool and a torque wrench.
steps.prose: This is printed under a heading reading FOR USE BY TRAINED GUNSMITHS ONLY, and the reason is structural: the shroud is keyed into the frame by a metal tab, so a standard barrel wrench twists the shroud and can take the frame with it. Nothing about routine cleaning requires the barrel to come out.
steps.quote: The stainless steel barrel tube must only be removed by a qualified gunsmith using a special tool available from Smith & Wesson. The barrel assembly is re-installed using the same tool and an accurate torque wrench.
steps.cite:
SAFETY & INSTRUCTION MANUAL

- Modern Style - J, K, L and N Frame - — p/n 416560000 REV:S&W_REVOLVER_112119 — Gunsmith Advisory, p.26

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: You have an open, empty cylinder and clean, inspected moon clips. That is everything this manual publishes for the Governor — the cylinder, yoke, hammer and lockwork stay in the frame and the barrel is gunsmith-only. Deep Clean carries the record of why for this listing.
steps.prose: The manual's own cleaning section tells you never to disassemble beyond its field-stripping and inspection instructions, which for this book means never past an open cylinder.
steps.quote: CAUTION: Never disassemble your firearm beyond the instructions in the Field Stripping and Inspection sections of this manual.
steps.cite:

deepAbsentReason: The J/K/L/N revolver manual documents inspecting, loading, firing, decocking, unloading, sight adjustment, moon-clip use and the Governor appendix, plus cleaning, maintenance and storage — and publishes no disassembly procedure of any kind. Its table of contents has no field-stripping section, and the only teardown it mentions, removal of the barrel tube, it assigns to a qualified gunsmith with a factory tool. Note that its p.30 caution refers the reader to 'the Field Stripping and Inspection sections of this manual', but no field-stripping section exists in it.

cleaning.name: BORE AND CHARGE HOLES
tasks: Remove excessive firing residue from the bore and every charge hole with a properly fitted brass brush dipped in gun cleaning solvent
Finish each with a dry cotton cloth patch to carry out residue and solvent
Clean the full length of each charge hole — a cylinder of 45 ACP or 45 Colt leaves a ring partway down a chamber bored for a 410 shell, and a shotshell will not seat past it
Clean the cylinder face, the moon clip recesses and the underside of the extractor star
If cases have been extracting hard, clean the charge holes thoroughly with solvent before changing ammunition brands

cleaning.name: MOON CLIPS
tasks: Pull each case straight out in the direction of the clip opening; prying the first one out relieves the tension on the rest
Inspect every clip and discard any that is broken, bent or cracked rather than straightening it
Use only two-round or full six-round clips — not half moon three-round clips
Replacement clips are available from Smith & Wesson dealers or Customer Service

cleaning.name: CYLINDER — IF YOURS IS TITANIUM ALLOY
tasks: Clean it with normal gun cleaning procedures, high quality gun oil and solvent where needed
Never use an abrasive on the charge holes or the front face — no sandpaper, abrasive pad or crocus cloth
Abrading the protective surface layer greatly shortens cylinder life and voids the warranty

cleaning.name: EXTERIOR, LUBRICATION AND STORAGE
tasks: Clean the exterior with a non-abrasive cloth and remove all cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints — finger moisture starts a corrosion process
Avoid prolonged solvent immersion and prolonged ultrasonic cleaning; never use ammoniated or strong alkaline solvents
After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts inside and out with a high quality gun oil
In a cold climate choose an oil weight that will not congeal and slow the action

For extended storage oil the bore, chambers and internal mechanism and coat the external mechanism and barrel with an anti-rust oil; do not store the revolver in leather or heavy cloth, or with a plug in the barrel
Check for signs of wear every time you clean it; if wear is noted, do not use the revolver

reassembly: Nothing was removed from the revolver, so there is nothing to reassemble — close the cylinder into the frame and confirm it locks.
Load stripped moon clips only when you are ready to shoot, pushing each cartridge straight in so the clip does not bend.
Clean the revolver again before firing if it has been in long storage.
fncheck: With every charge hole confirmed empty and the bore clear, close the cylinder and check that it latches and that the thumbpiece releases it cleanly. Cycle the action double action and single action pointed in a safe direction, confirming the cylinder indexes and locks at each stop and that the hammer returns fully to the at-rest forward position rather than stopping partway. Then seat an empty two-round moon clip and confirm it sits flush in its recesses and the cylinder still closes without force.
